This project develops mismatch-aware fine-mapping for GWAS summary statistics
analyzed with external reference LD. Its goals are to measure mismatch, recover
reference-LD SuSiE-RSS when the inputs are matched, and avoid spurious
additional signals when they are mismatched.

When the mismatch-aware fit returns zero or one deduplicated,
purity-passing credible set, the operational procedure reports a 95% credible
set from a single-effect RSS refit using only the unit diagonal. This fallback
is a locus-level summary for loci already established as associated; it does
not test association or assert that exactly one causal variant is present.

## Reproducible paper experiments

The primary simulation uses reproducible coalescent reference LD generated
with `stdpopsim` and `msprime`; in-sample
LD and summary statistics are then generated from the SuSiE-IW model. The study
crosses one, two and three true effects with a range of true mismatch
concentrations and compares in-sample SuSiE-RSS, reference-LD SuSiE-RSS,
collapsed-R and AIW-N.

Run the full concentration calibration, independent performance benchmark,
summaries and paper figures with:

```bash
Rscript --vanilla experiments/run-paper-coalescent-experiments.R
```

Worker-level results are checkpointed, so the command resumes completed jobs
after interruption. The principal numerical summary is in
`experiments/coalescent-susie-iw-benchmark-report.md`; the complete design and
frozen calibration constants are documented in the supplementary manuscript.

Earlier development experiments are retained in a local-only archive and are
not invoked by the current manuscript workflows.
